title: nginx 1.10.3 (EOL) running on ports 80 and 443
description: nginx 1.10.3 on Ubuntu is end-of-life. Vulnerable to CVE-2017-7529 (range filter integer overflow), CVE-2019-9511-9518 etc.
risks: Remote code execution, info disclosure, request smuggling possible via known nginx CVEs.
attack_vectors: Exploit CVE-2017-7529 to leak cache data via Range header integer overflow. Test for HTTP request smuggling.
proof_of_existence:
PORT STATE SERVICE VERSION
80/tcp open http nginx 1.10.3 (Ubuntu)
443/tcp open ssl/http nginx 1.10.3 (Ubuntu)
|_http-server-header: nginx/1.10.3 (Ubuntu)
remediation: Upgrade nginx to latest stable version (1.25+) immediately.

title: OpenSSH 7.2p2 (EOL) on port 22 with publickey-only auth
description: OpenSSH 7.2p2 Ubuntu 4ubuntu2.8 is outdated. Multiple CVEs including user enumeration (CVE-2018-15473). Auth limited to publickey.
risks: SSH user enumeration, potential privilege escalation via known exploits. Weak key algorithms may be accepted.
attack_vectors: Attempt CVE-2018-15473 user enumeration. Check for weak SSH host key algorithms. Bruteforce key acceptance.
proof_of_existence: 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 7.2p2 Ubuntu 4ubuntu2.8\nssh-hostkey: 2048 RSA, 256 ECDSA, 256 ED25519\nssh-auth-methods: Supported: publickey
remediation: Upgrade OpenSSH to 9.x+ and disable legacy key exchange algorithms.

title: Deprecated TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 enabled with weak 1024-bit DH
description: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated (RFC 8996). DH key exchange uses only 1024-bit, lower than cert key strength. CBC ciphers enabled.
risks: Downgrade attacks, BEAST, POODLE, CRIME. Weak DH enables logjam-style attacks. Compliance violations (PCI-DSS).
attack_vectors: Force TLS 1.0 downgrade. Exploit weak DH via Logjam attack. Use BEAST/POODLE against CBC ciphers.
proof_of_existence: TLSv1.0: ciphers incl CBC SHA, DH 1024. TLSv1.1: same. Warnings: Key exchange (dh 1024) lower strength than cert key. No TLS 1.3.
remediation: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1, enable TLS 1.2/1.3 only, use 2048+ bit DH, prefer GCM ciphers.

title: robots.txt exposes 84 disallowed PrestaShop URL patterns
description: robots.txt contains 84 disallowed entries with PrestaShop-specific patterns: order, q, page, orderby, orderway, tag, id_currency, search_query.
risks: Information leakage of application structure and parameters. Aids targeted enumeration of admin/api endpoints.
attack_vectors: Use disallowed patterns to enumerate PrestaShop modules, admin paths, and API endpoints for version fingerprinting.
remediation: Restrict robots.txt to non-sensitive patterns. Don't expose internal parameter names.

title: Only 34.76.215.208 responsive; other IPs appear down or filtered
description: 34.77.166.175 showed no open ports in targeted scans. 193.203.239.21 reported host down by nmap. Only 34.76.215.208 has services.
risks: Reduced attack surface but may indicate firewall filtering or decommissioned services on other IPs.
attack_vectors: Retry with -Pn flag for 193.203.239.21. Use masscan for faster full-port discovery on all IPs.
proof_of_existence: 34.77.166.175: no open ports in HTTP/SSL scans. 193.203.239.21: 'Host seems down. If really up but blocking ping, try -Pn'
remediation: Verify if 34.77.166.175 and 193.203.239.21 are still active. Use -Pn for ICMP-blocked hosts.

title: UDP scan inconclusive — all ports open|filtered
description: UDP scan of 11 common ports (53,67,69,123,161,162,500,514,1900,4500,5353) returned open|filtered for all. No definitive open UDP.
risks: Potential UDP services (SNMP, DNS, TFTP) may be running but firewalled. SNMP could expose system info.
attack_vectors: Send protocol-specific UDP probes (SNMP get-request, DNS version.bind) to confirm services.
proof_of_existence: 53/udp open|filtered domain, 67/udp open|filtered dhcps, 161/udp open|filtered snmp, 514/udp open|filtered syslog, 5353/udp open|filtered zeroconf
remediation: Run targeted UDP probes with application-specific payloads to confirm services.

title: Full TCP port scan timed out — incomplete port coverage
description: nmap -p- (65535 ports) timed out after 180s across 3 IPs. Only targeted port scans succeeded. Many ports unscanned.
risks: Unknown services on non-standard ports may be missed. Hidden admin panels, databases, or dev ports undetected.
attack_vectors: Use masscan or rustscan for faster full-port enumeration. Target specific high-risk ports (3306, 6379, 27017, 9200).
proof_of_existence: Exit Code: -1, Duration: 180.11s, STDOUT: (empty) — command timed out after 180s
remediation: Use masscan for fast port discovery, then nmap for service version detection on found ports.

title: HTTP redirects to non-HTTPS on port 443
description: Port 443 SSL response redirects to http://playtunisie.com/ (non-SSL). TLS connection available but site forces plaintext HTTP.
risks: TLS termination without enforcement. User sessions exposed to MITM. No HSTS header protection.
attack_vectors: Intercept HTTP traffic via MITM. Strip SSL since no HSTS. Capture session cookies in plaintext.
proof_of_existence: 443/tcp open ssl/http nginx 1.10.3 | http-headers: Location: http://playtunisie.com/ | (Request type: GET)
remediation: Enforce HTTPS-only with 301 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS. Add HSTS header with preload.

title: Web scanning tools timed out — possible rate limiting or blocking
description: WhatWeb and Nikto both timed out after 80-120s with no response on both playtunisie.com and blog.playtunisie.com. nmap HTTP scripts succeeded on IP.
risks: May indicate WAF/IPS blocking scanning tools, or slow application response. Hinders vulnerability assessment.
attack_vectors: Use slower scan rates, different user agents, or scan via IP instead of hostname. Try ffuf with rate limiting.
poc: whatweb -a 3 https://playtunisie.com (timed out); nikto -h https://playtunisie.com -maxtime 120 (no web server found)
proof_of_existence: whatweb: ERROR Opening: https://playtunisie.com - execution expired. nikto: No web server found on playtunisie.com:443. Max execution time reached.
remediation: Investigate if WAF/IPS is blocking scanner user-agents. Whitelist authorized testing IPs.

title: No SMB/NetBIOS ports open on any target IP
description: SMB scan (ports 445, 139) across all 3 IPs returned 0 hosts up. No Windows file sharing exposed.
risks: Low risk — no SMB attack surface. Confirms Linux-only infrastructure.
proof_of_existence: Nmap done: 3 IP addresses (0 hosts up) scanned in 5.14 seconds

title: All TCP ports filtered on primary web server (34.76.215.208)
description: Full TCP scan of all 65535 ports shows every port in filtered state. Host is up but firewall blocks all direct connections. Google Cloud load balancer likely fronts the service.
risks: Limited attack surface exposure; only CDN/LB ports accessible externally.
attack_vectors: Direct port scanning ineffective; must target via domain name through CDN. Previous cycle found 443 open via domain.
proof_of_existence: All 65535 scanned ports on 208.215.76.34.bc.googleusercontent.com (34.76.215.208) are in ignored states. Not shown: 65535 filtered tcp ports (no-response)
remediation: Maintain firewall rules; ensure only load balancer ports 80/443 are exposed.

title: All TCP ports filtered on mail server (193.203.239.21)
description: Full TCP scan of mail45.lwspanel.com shows all 65535 ports filtered. No mail/FTP services accessible from external scan. Host is up but fully firewalled.
risks: Mail services inaccessible externally; may indicate services are internal-only or behind different access controls.
attack_vectors: Cannot exploit mail/FTP services directly; would need VPN or internal network access. DNS records point to this host for mail.
proof_of_existence: All 65535 scanned ports on mail45.lwspanel.com (193.203.239.21) are in ignored states. Not shown: 65535 filtered tcp ports (no-response)
remediation: Maintain firewall; ensure mail ports only accessible from trusted networks.

title: Mail/FTP services (ports 21,25,110,143,465,587,993,995) all filtered
description: Targeted scan of common mail and FTP ports on mail45.lwspanel.com shows all ports filtered. NSE scripts (ftp-anon, smtp-open-relay, etc.) could not execute.
risks: Cannot assess mail server security posture; services may exist but are firewalled.
attack_vectors: No direct attack vector from external network. Would need to bypass firewall or access via internal network.
proof_of_existence: 21/tcp filtered ftp, 25/tcp filtered smtp, 110/tcp filtered pop3, 143/tcp filtered imap, 465/tcp filtered smtps, 587/tcp filtered submission, 993/tcp filtered imaps, 995/tcp filtered pop3s
remediation: Restrict mail/FTP ports to authorized IPs only; disable unused services.

title: UDP ports open|filtered — inconclusive on both hosts
description: UDP scan of 6 common ports shows all as open|filtered on both hosts. Cannot confirm if services are actually running or if firewall drops UDP probes.
risks: Potential DNS, NTP, SNMP, or IKE services may be running but undetectable due to filtering.
attack_vectors: If SNMP is running, community string brute-force could reveal system info. If DNS, zone transfer or cache poisoning attempts.
proof_of_existence: 53/udp open|filtered domain, 123/udp open|filtered ntp, 137/udp open|filtered netbios-ns, 138/udp open|filtered netbios-dgm, 161/udp open|filtered snmp, 500/udp open|filtered isakmp
remediation: Block unnecessary UDP ports at firewall; disable SNMP if not needed.

title: Web application scanning tools consistently timeout against playtunisie.com
description: WhatWeb, Nikto, and dirb all timed out or found no web server on port 443. Site may have WAF, rate limiting, or very slow response times blocking automated scanning.
risks: Unable to fingerprint web technologies, enumerate directories, or identify web vulnerabilities via automated tools.
attack_vectors: Manual browsing or slow, rate-limited requests may bypass protections. Previous cycle confirmed nginx 1.10.3 via curl.
poc: whatweb -a 3 https://playtunisie.com; nikto -h https://playtunisie.com -timeout 10 -maxtime 120; dirb https://playtunisie.com
proof_of_existence: whatweb: execution expired. Nikto: No web server found on playtunisie.com:443. dirb: FATAL: Too many errors connecting to host (OPERATION TIMEOUT).
remediation: Investigate why web tools timeout; check for WAF rules or server response latency.

title: SNMP service undetectable — port 161 filtered
description: SNMP TCP port 161 filtered on both hosts. UDP scan showed open|filtered. Cannot confirm SNMP service or enumerate community strings.
risks: If SNMP is running with default community strings, it could expose system information and configuration data.
attack_vectors: SNMP enumeration with tools like snmpwalk if community string is known/default (public/private).
proof_of_existence: 161/tcp filtered snmp (both hosts). UDP scan: 161/udp open|filtered snmp (both hosts).
remediation: Disable SNMP if unused; use SNMPv3 with strong credentials if needed.

title: SSL/TLS cipher enumeration blocked — port 443 filtered via direct IP
description: Direct nmap scan to IP 34.76.215.208 on port 443 shows filtered. SSL cert and cipher enumeration scripts could not run. Previous cycle identified weak TLS via domain-based curl.
risks: Cannot fully enumerate TLS configuration via direct IP; must rely on domain-based assessment.
attack_vectors: Use domain name (playtunisie.com) instead of direct IP to assess TLS configuration, as CDN/LB terminates connections.
remediation: Use SNI-based scanning via domain name; ensure TLS configuration on CDN/LB is hardened.

title: Target infrastructure behind Google Cloud with aggressive firewall filtering
description: Host resolves to Google Cloud Compute Engine (bc.googleusercontent.com). All ports filtered except via CDN/LB path. OS fingerprinting inconclusive (too many matches).
risks: Attack surface is minimal; only web application via domain name is exposed. Backend services fully firewalled.
attack_vectors: Focus on web application layer vulnerabilities via domain name. CDN bypass (origin IP leak) could expose backend directly.
proof_of_existence: 208.215.76.34.bc.googleusercontent.com. All 65535 filtered. Too many fingerprints match this host to give specific OS details.
remediation: Ensure Google Cloud firewall rules restrict all non-essential traffic; use Cloud CDN/WAF.
